title: Rate adaptor translation failure leading to credit saturation and customer throttles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A translation bug in the rate-adaptor component converted burst policy 'window' units incorrectly when translating from Control Plane policy objects to the runtime token-bucket configuration. The bug caused Dedicated and some Private tenants (and a small subset of Hosted customers routed through the legacy adaptor) to have 10x shorter effective burst windows, which saturated per-tenant credits and produced opaque 429s for affected customers.

Scope & impact: 7 customers reported increased 429s during business hours across Hosted/Dedicated/Private configurations. Symptoms included sudden latency spikes followed by sustained quota rejections. Customers reported degraded user experiences and several escalations to Solutions/Support.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-05 03:22 UTC: First pager from SRE for elevated tenant 429 rate (internal monitoring alert).
- 2026-03-05 03:35 UTC: Triage plus initial mitigation: enabled conservative global fallback policy (throttle to low-rate but fixed window) to reduce blast radius.
- 2026-03-05 04:10 UTC: Identified mismatched field mapping in rate-adaptor (window_ms vs window_seconds) introduced during an earlier policy migration change.
- 2026-03-05 06:00 UTC: Hotfix deployed to control-plane translate layer (PR linked below) and a live config backfill script executed for impacted tenants.
- 2026-03-05 08:30 UTC: Customer-facing incidents started to clear; monitoring showed token buckets returning to expected behavior.

Root cause: The control-plane to runtime translation layer (rate-adaptor) expected burst.window to be expressed in milliseconds for newer model schemas but accepted seconds for older schemas. A recent migration that normalized schema keys introduced an implicit conversion for new tenants but missed legacy tenant objects. For affected tenants translation applied value as-is, turning e.g., 60000s into 60000ms, effectively reducing the window by 1000x in some rare combinations and causing credits to deplete much faster. The code path was exercised when customers used Dedicated with older policy objects or when a private deployment used the legacy config importer.

Immediate mitigation & fix:
- Rolled back the heuristic introduced in the migration that removed explicit unit tags.
- Deployed runtime-2.4.1 containing defensive checks and a safe-parse step in the rate-adaptor.
- Executed a one-off backfill job (id: backfill-20260305-01) to retranslate and patch impacted tenant configs.
- Restored per-tenant temporary emergency credit pools for the highest-severity customers for 48 hours to prevent rethrottling during verification.

Verification & monitoring:
- Added alerting on mismatch ratio between control-plane-config.window and runtime-applied.window for all tenants.
- Dashboards updated: token-bucket-consumption, control-runtime-translation-errors (links below).
- Verified with 24h of noise-free metrics and customer confirmations.

Communications:
- Customer emails and support threads updated; SRE/Success ran focused reconnects with top impacted accounts.
- Incident postmortem created and shared (link below).

Artifacts & links:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-control/pull/1294
- Backfill job: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/backfill-20260305-01
- Incident postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-03-05+Rate+Adaptor+Translation+Outage
- Dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tokbucket/translation-telemetry

Follow-ups (action items):
1) Add strict schema validation on ingestion path for policy objects with explicit unit normalization (owner: Sofia).
2) End-to-end integration test that cross-checks control-plane payload, rate-adaptor translation, and runtime applied config (owner: Eng/runtime).
3) Extend migration tooling with reversible audit logs and preflight checks (owner: Migration team).
4) Update runbooks for on-call to include quick backfill/playbook and emergency credit restoration steps (owner: SRE).
5) Customer-facing: offer credits or SL credits to top impacted customers (owner: Customer Success).

Notes: This ticket includes the implemented code changes and verification artifacts. Follow-ups are tracked in separate tickets; see dependencies.
